title: Isolation and analysis of fractions enriched in WrappER-associated mitochondria from mouse liver
protocol: Prepare all the buffers and cool down the centrifuge to 4°C.
Transfer 11 mL of B10 buffer to a 15 mL Falcon tube.
Add 110 μL of protease inhibitor cocktail (PIC) without EDTA to the B10 buffer in the Falcon tube.
Transfer 15 mL of B10 buffer to a 50 mL glass beaker.
Keep the glass beaker containing B10 buffer on ice.
Euthanize the mouse.
Incise the abdomen with surgical scissors to expose the liver.
Excise the liver, discard the gallbladder, and transfer it to the 50 mL glass beaker.
Cut the liver into small pieces using clean surgical scissors.
Rinse three times with 15 mL of B10 to remove blood.
Tilt the beaker to let the small liver pieces decant, then remove most of the buffer by gently tilting the beaker again.
Use a P1000 pipette to remove the last few milliliters of B10.
Add 4 mL of B10PIC to the chopped, rinsed liver and transfer it into the modified 5 mL Teflon Potter by tilting the beaker.
Assist in transferring small liver pieces using surgical scissors or a wooden spatula if necessary.
Do not fill the potter past the fill line; remove excess buffer with a P1000 if necessary.
Place the modified glass potter with the chopped liver inside a 50 mL Falcon tube containing ice.
Keep the glass potter cold during liver homogenization.
Use an electric homogenizer to homogenize the liver by stroking up and down the potter at 1,600 rpm for 8 up strokes and 8 down strokes (2 seconds per stroke), then pause for 30 seconds.
Repeat the homogenizing step as described in the previous instruction.
Transfer the liver homogenate to a 15 mL Falcon tube by tilting the glass potter.
Rinse the potter with the remaining 7 mL of cold B10PIC and add them to the liver homogenate.
Mix gently by inverting the tube a few times.
Pour the homogenate into two 30 mL glass centrifuge tubes.
Spin at 400 × g for 10 min at 4°C to remove nuclei and tissue debris.
Collect the supernatant (approximately 5 mL per tube) and transfer it to a clean 30 mL glass centrifuge tube.
Repeat steps 12 and 13 one more time.
Pour 7 mL of B27 into a 50 mL Falcon tube.
Carefully layer 7 mL of post-nuclear hepatic homogenate on top of the B27.
Spin at 2,000 × g for 20 min at 4°C.
Add 7 mL of B27 into a 50 mL Falcon tube.
Gently layer 7 mL of post-nuclear liver homogenate on top of the B27.
Centrifuge the solution in a fixed rotor F34-6-38 for Eppendorf centrifuge 5800.
Thoroughly remove the supernatant using a disposable glass Pasteur pipette connected to the vacuum line.
Collect the top 5 mL of the supernatant to prepare the control ER-enriched fraction.
Resuspend the pellet in 500 μL B10PIC for omics analysis and store at -80°C.
For Electron Microscopy (EM) analysis, gently add 500 μL of B27PIC on top of the pellet.
Using a paintbrush, gently detach the pellet from the side of the tube.
Spin the sample at 12,000 × g for 10 minutes at 4°C to remove heavy organelles.
Collect the supernatant using a P1000 pipette tip and transfer into two clean Eppendorf tubes.
Repeat the centrifugation step to further purify the ER-enriched fraction.
Combine 1.5 ml of supernatant from each tube into a single Falcon tube.
Add 22.5 ml of ice-cold CaCl2 solution at 8 mM concentration and incubate for 15 minutes at 4°C with gentle rocking.
Pour the mixture gently into two glass tubes (12 ml per tube) and centrifuge at 8,000 × g for 10 minutes at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant and retain the pellet as the ER-enriched fraction.
Resuspend the pellet in 500 μL B10PIC.
Store the sample at −80°C for omics analysis.
Gently add 500 μL of B27PIC on top of the pellet for Electron Microscopy (EM) analysis.
Using a paintbrush, gently detach the pellet from the side of the tube.
Transfer the flaky pellet into a 2 mL Eppendorf tube with a round bottom.
Add 500 μL of B27PIC to the tube.
Use a P200 pipette tip cut ∼5 mm from the end to enlarge the opening for handling the flaky pellet.
Spin the sample at 3,000 × g for 10 minutes at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant.
Gently add 500 μL of B27 solution supplemented with 2% glutaraldehyde to the pellet.
Incubate overnight (16 hours) at 4°C.
Remove the glutaraldehyde solution carefully using a plastic transfer pipette, ensuring the pellet remains intact.
Rinse the pellet three times by gently applying 700 μL of B27 solution onto the wall of the Eppendorf tube.
Incubate the pellet in a solution of 1% (w/v) osmium tetroxide in ddH2O for 30 minutes at 20°C, protecting from light with aluminum foil.

Reconstitute Durcupan epoxy resin by adding 5 g of Durcupan component A, 5 g of Durcupan component B, 0.15 g of Durcupan component C, and 0.15 g of Durcupan component D in a 50 mL plastic beaker placed on a scale.
Stir well with a wooden spatula until the resin changes color and becomes orange.
Store reconstituted Durcupan epoxy resin for up to 2 weeks at -20°C if not used immediately.
Rinse the pellet three times using ddH2O in an Eppendorf tube.
Add 1 ml of 50% ethanol:water and incubate for 15 min.
Discard the ethanol solution after incubation.
Add 1 ml of 1% uranyl acetate in 70% ethanol:water and incubate for 40 min protected from light with aluminum foil.
Remove and discard the uranyl acetate solution.
Add 1 ml of 90% ethanol:water and incubate for 15 min.
Discard the ethanol solution after incubation.
Add 1 ml of 100% ethanol and incubate for 15 min.
Discard the ethanol solution after incubation.
Repeat step of adding 1 ml of 100% ethanol and incubating for 15 min.
Add 1 ml of 100% propylene oxide to the pellet and incubate for 15 min.
Discard the propylene oxide after incubation.
Repeat the step of adding 1 ml of 100% propylene oxide and incubating for 15 min.
Embed the pellet in the Durcupan epoxy resin.
Leave the cap of the Eppendorf tube open.
Remove and discard the 100% propylene oxide.
Quickly embed the pellet in approximately 500 μL of reconstituted Durcupan epoxy resin.
Incubate for 1 hour at 37°C.
Remove as much epoxy resin as possible, leaving the pellet undisturbed.
Add 500 μL of epoxy resin.
Move the sample into an oven at 58°C.
Incubate for 48–72 hours to polymerize the reconstituted Durcupan epoxy resin.
Release the hardened epoxy resin block containing the sample by cutting the Eppendorf tube with a sharp blade or scissors.
Cut the epoxy resin-embedded sample into approximately 50 nm thick slices using a Leica Ultramicrotome.
Place up to five slices on single-slot formvar coated copper grids.
Counterstain the slices by incubating the grid for 5 minutes with Reynold’s lead citrate.
